result.title: Kolibri: Color Finds the Place, Refinement Sets the Pose for RGB-D Localization in Colored Point Clouds
result.summary: An agent or robot in a scanned building must locate its camera in rooms that no model saw during training. Point cloud registration methods can align each RGB-D frame with the building's colored point cloud, accurately but at a high cost. We observe that geometric refinement brings nearby initial poses to the same final pose, so the learned component only needs to find the place. Kolibri does this with a graph network of 55,712 parameters that describes 10 cm cubes of points, called cells, by their color, local shape and neighbors. With the same refinement, it matches GeDi on 96 unseen ScanNet rooms (81.4% against 80.3% within 5 cm and 5°) and on a held-out test of 10 further rooms, in 82 ms per frame on an RTX 2080 Ti. The saved time allows for search without a room label. In one point cloud of 100 rooms, Kolibri loses 1.3 points against knowing the room, while retrieving the room first loses 56.0. In a hospital emergency department scene from a real scan, it localizes 86.5% of the frames rendered from the scan in 384 ms each, where GeDi needs 91 minutes per frame on cubes of the scan for a similar recall. The method needs colors that agree between the frame and the point cloud. On gray frames and across cameras with different color responses, point cloud registration methods keep the lead.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Kolibri：用仅 5.5 万参数的图网络描述彩色点云中 10cm 体素的颜色、局部形状与邻域，仅做「找位置」的初始位姿预测，再交由几何精配准完成 6DoF 定位，实现无需房间标签的快速 RGB-D 重定位。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把任务分解为廉价的粗候选检索与昂贵的几何精化，并考察跨房间/跨相机的外观一致性失效，可供核查 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK 的贡献分配、视觉证据筛选与计算成本权衡是否有类比价值。
